transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-06
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel, Ethan Ruiz (Redwood) | Lina Zhou, Marcus Green, Priya Nair, Diego Ramos (Sparrow AI)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria, security/compliance gates (SOC 2 / ISO / SSO/SAML / RBAC / audit logs), workload sizing and benchmark plan, and timeline to pilot. Focus on what Sparrow needs to greenlight pilot and what Redwood needs to run realistic throughput tests.

Topics:
- Acceptance criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy tolerances)
- Security docs and SSO integration approach
- Audit log retention and encryption/KMS questions
- Benchmarking plan and sample dataset/workload
- Pilot timeline and resources

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll—uh—kick off. quick intros?
[00:08] Lina Zhou: yeah i'm lina, head of ml at sparrow, we run recommendation and instruction tuning models, we're exploring hosted and dedicated for a three week pilot.
[00:15] Marcus Green: Marcus here, CTO, i'll be focused on compliance and infra impact.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Priya, security engineer, i'll own SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit requirements.
[00:25] Samira Patel: awesome, ethan and i from Redwood, ethan will cover perf and benching.
[00:28] Ethan Ruiz: hi all.
[00:30] [00:30] Ethan Ruiz: quick agenda — success criteria, workload matrix, security gates, timeline. sound right?
[00:36] Lina Zhou: yes — and costs per token, we need ballpark for pilot so we can budget.
[00:40] Samira Patel: we'll include pilot pricing options in follow up, ok starting with success criteria — can you share what would be a pass/fail for you for this POC?
[00:50] Marcus Green: security first — we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary. For the pilot we need SSO via SAML and role-based access so that only the ML team can spin up endpoints, ops can see logs, and auditors can pull logs. audit retention requirement is 12 months initially.
[01:05] Priya Nair: to add, we also need proof of encryption at rest via KMS or HSM, and ability to rotate keys. also detailed audit trails with user/activity mapping and request/response hashes — we may redact payloads but need request ids and metadata.
[01:20] Ethan Ruiz: yes we support KMS integrated enclaves and rotation. we'll attach our KMS integration doc. audit logs are exportable to S3 or customer SIEM, retention configurable. default retention is 90 days on hosted, can extend for Dedicated or Private.
[01:34] Priya Nair: ok extension to 12 months must be part of pilot scope — either via export or Dedicated plan.
[01:40] Samira Patel: noted. on SSO — we support SAML/Okta, SCIM provisioning for users, and per-route RBAC. what roles do you want?
[01:50] Diego Ramos: minimally admin, operator, reader, and developer. developers should be able to create test endpoints but not modify billing. ops should see logs and set retention.
[01:59] Lina Zhou: and we need API keys with scoped permissions for service accounts — ability to rotate and revoke.
[02:06] Ethan Ruiz: we have API keys, and token-based service accounts with expiry. rotation is supported via the console or API. we'll show that in demo.
[02:12] [02:12] Ethan Ruiz: moving to workload sizing — Lina, what model sizes and seq lengths?
[02:18] Lina Zhou: two main workloads: short-chats for UI assistant (avg 180 tokens, peak 512) and long reasoning for batch rerank (avg 1,200 tokens, peak 4k). throughput target for chat is 200 rps at p50 < 120ms and p95 < 300ms. for batch rerank we need 50 concurrent requests with 4k sequence and p95 < 1.2s per chunk — maybe explore batching.
[02:43] Ethan Ruiz: good, we'll map that to GPUs and batching. for POC we'll run two bench types: interactive load (200 rps, mixed 180-512 tokens) and long sequences (50 concurrent, 1.2k-4k). we'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:58] Marcus Green: and fallback policy — if Dedicated underprovisions, can we route to hosted? we need predictable cost behavior and graceful degradation.
[03:06] Samira Patel: yes, routing/fallback is supported; we'll outline cost delta.
[03:09] Priya Nair: audit and data residency — we must ensure logs don't leak content. do you offer payload redaction hooks before export?
[03:16] Ethan Ruiz: we support configurable sanitization filters and can hash or redact fields. we also provide per-request metadata and request/response size, but raw content redaction is doable before it's stored long-term.
[03:26] [03:26] Lina Zhou: on acceptance — beyond perf, product quality thresholds: correct ranking lift of at least 7% for rerank tests vs baseline, and hallucination rate below 2% on a supplied eval set.
[03:37] Ethan Ruiz: we can run evals against your prompt set; Redwood Optimize will generate quantization and batching recs and surface quality deltas.
[03:44] Samira Patel: timeline — what's your target to start the pilot?
[03:47] Marcus Green: ideally two weeks from now, but realistically we need time for SAML integration and legal review — 10/20 is target week.
[03:55] Samira Patel: ok we'll aim for week of 2026-10-20 for the pilot run. Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO docs and a short security questionnaire to speed legal.
[04:05] Priya Nair: about the questionnaire — we'll need contact for pen test scheduling and details about your encryption modules and whether we can get a read-only view of infra configuration in Dedicated.
[04:15] Ethan Ruiz: SEs can provide architecture diagrams, and for Dedicated we can arrange a constrained read-only dashboard. pen test coordination — we have an approval process, we'll share that flow.
[04:25] [04:25] Lina Zhou: for the benchmark dataset, we'll provide 500 sample user queries representative of chat and 1k documents for rerank. would you like a synthetic load or real-ish traces?
[04:36] Ethan Ruiz: both helps. synthetic for stress, traces for quality profiling. we'll ask for CSV of traces and a schema.
[04:42] Samira Patel: ok next steps recapped: ethan will run an initial perf script, samira will share security pack, priya will send SAML metadata and roles, and we'll schedule pilot week of 10/20.
[04:55] Marcus Green: also send a short list of minimum per-route RBAC checks and the audit log fields you'll capture.
[05:02] Priya Nair: verify that logs include: request id, timestamp, user id, action type, model id, model version, latency, error codes, and optional hashed payload id.
[05:14] Ethan Ruiz: yes that's the standard; we'll confirm exact names.
[05:18] Samira Patel: any other blockers?
[05:20] Lina Zhou: just pricing — show pilot options and two pathways: hosted pilot vs dedicated reserved capacity recommendation.
[05:27] Samira Patel: will do.
[05:29] [05:29] Diego Ramos: one last note on networking — for Dedicated we need VPC peering with our subnet and egress controls. for hosted we need IP allowlist for callbacks.
[05:40] Ethan Ruiz: supported. we'll include networking checklist in the follow up.
[05:45] Samira Patel: cool, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[05:50] Marcus Green: thanks, talk soon.
[05:52] [End of recording]
